ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of the device for “using a mass spectrometer to determine the mass of charged particles.” In the velocity selector, the direction of the field strength E is vertically downward, the direction of the magnetic induction intensity B1 is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and the direction of the magnetic induction intensity B2 in the separator is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. At S there are four monovalent positive ions, Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding, incident into the velocity selector perpendicular to E and B1. If their mass relationship satisfies mJia=mYi<mBing=mDing, their velocity relationship satisfies vJia<vYi=vBing<vDing, and gravity can all be ignored. Please write, in the order of P1, P2, P3, P4, the ions that hit each point respectively.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure is a schematic diagram of the device for “using a mass spectrometer to determine the mass of charged particles.” In the velocity selector, the direction of the field strength E is vertically downward, the direction of the magnetic induction intensity B1 is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, and the direction of the magnetic induction intensity B2 in the separator is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. At S there are four monovalent positive ions, Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding, incident into the velocity selector perpendicular to E and B1. If their mass relationship satisfies mJia=mYi<mBing=mDing, their velocity relationship satisfies vJia<vYi=vBing<vDing, and gravity can all be ignored. Please write, in the order of P1, P2, P3, P4, the ions that hit each point respectively.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the velocity selector, S is on its left side, and the ions enter from S horizontally to the right; inside the selector is marked a downward electric field E, the upper plate is positive, the lower plate is negative, and the magnetic field B1 is represented by crosses, indicating perpendicular to the paper surface inward. On the right side of the selector there are two blocking points/exits, upper and lower, labeled P2 and P1, among which P2 is above and P1 is below. On the right side is the separator region, the magnetic field B2 is represented by dots, indicating perpendicular to the paper surface outward; after the ions passing through the selector enter the right side, they move along downward-curving semicircular trajectories and hit respectively the higher P3 and the lower P4 on the vertical receiving plate. Then reason: When positive ions move to the right, the direction of the electric field force they receive in the velocity selector is downward; because B1 is perpendicular to the paper surface inward, according to the left-hand rule, the direction of the Lorentz force is upward. The condition for passing straight through the velocity selector is qvB1=qE, that is, v=E/B1. If the velocity is smaller, then the magnetic force qvB1 is less than the electric field force qE, the ion deflects downward and hits the lower P1; if the velocity is larger, then the magnetic force is greater than the electric field force, the ion deflects upward and hits the upper P2. In the problem vJia<vYi=vBing<vDing, those that can pass straight through together should be Yi and Bing with the same velocity, so Jia is the low-speed particle that hits P1, Ding is the high-speed particle that hits P2, and Yi and Bing enter the separator. In the separator, Yi and Bing are both monovalent positive ions, their velocities upon entering are the same, and the magnetic field B2 is the same. The radius of circular motion is r=mv/(qB2), so the radius is proportional to the mass. Also mYi<mBing, so Yi has a smaller radius and hits the higher P3; Bing has a larger radius and hits the lower P4. In the order of P1, P2, P3, P4, it is: Jia, Ding, Yi, Bing.
